newsitem.title: USA: Bill introduced to cut U.S. tobacco subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Bill introduced to cut U.S. tobacco subsidies.

text.p: A bipartisan bill to cut federal subsidies for tobacco farmers was introduced Thursday in the U.S. House of Representatives and the Senate.
"The federal government has no business underwriting this deadly product," Sen. Dick Durbin, an Illinois Democrat, told a news conference.

He said his bill would end the federal subsidy which makes up the difference between farmer-paid crop insurance premiums and payouts for tobacco crop losses, But it would not affect the federal tobacco price support programme.
Other co-sponsors of the bill were Sens. Judd Gregg, a New Hampshire Republican, and Frank Lautenberg, a New Jersey Democrat, and Representative Diana DeGette, a Colorado Democrat.
They said the government was expected to spend $67 million in tobacco subsidies this year compared to $97 million last year.
